ai.description: The Sabarimala Night Frog is a small amphibian (20–25 mm) with a brown, warty dorsum and pale yellow belly. It features a distinct, pointed snout and prominent, fleshy femoral glands.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus sabarimalai* is best distinguished by its unique, significantly elongated third finger, which is notably longer than those of other *Nyctibatrachus* species.
ai.habitat: The Sabarimala Night Frog inhabits evergreen forests in the southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 400 and 900 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sabarimala Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small invertebrates along the rocky, moss-covered stream banks of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Sabarimala Night Frog breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of 15–20 eggs on wet rocks, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sabarimala night frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 400 and 900 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Sabarimala Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes, typically heard calling from moss-covered rocks near fast-flowing streams.
